title: Sheet Number Authority Resolver and CDE Pre-Registration Gate
purpose: Resolve the applicable sheet/drawing numbering authority, acquire missing project data through governed AI inquiry, classify document meaning independently from identifier syntax, and prevent ambiguous or unauthorized identities from entering a governed CDE document register.

ai_inquiry.principle: The AI shall retrieve or ask for facts; it shall not invent project codes, mappings, or authority.
question_policy: Do not ask the user for a value already resolved by higher-precedence project evidence.
When evidence contains one unambiguous applicable value, normalize it and echo the value and source back for confirmation where interpretation was required.
When evidence contains conflicting values, present the conflict and ask the user to identify the governing value or provide the governing source; do not choose silently.
When evidence is silent, ask one focused question for the missing value and explain why it is needed.
A user answer may establish a project fact for the current workflow, but shall not be represented as an external-standard, client-enterprise, or contractual requirement unless supported by evidence.
If the user says a value will be provided, capture it before proceeding rather than converting it to TBC without another prompt.
Persist confirmed answers in the structured project semantic record so subsequent sheets reuse them and the user is not repeatedly asked.
Public TIVERIT examples and conformance cases shall anonymize real project/client identifiers using neutral placeholders such as AAA, WWW, ZZZ, Project A, Client A, Building A, Zone A, or equivalent.

inquiry_groups.purpose: Determine which numbering rules govern the project.
Capture project-wide values normally reused across many sheets.
Resolve project spatial identity where required by the selected profile.
Classify the individual sheet without conflating meaning with its final number.
Resolve values required for formal document registration.

example_dialogue_logic: AI: I found a project BEP. I will use it first for project-specific sheet-numbering values and ask only for unresolved fields.

AI: The BEP identifies a project phase, but I do not yet have governing evidence for whether that phase belongs inside the CDE document number. I will keep it as project-phase metadata unless the document-control rule says otherwise.

AI: This sheet appears to be an enlarged floor plan. Is it an enlargement of a room/area, or merely one part of an overall floor plan split across multiple sheets? This determines the content subtype.

AI: I cannot establish the required governed-CDE document-number grammar from the available project evidence. Please provide or identify the document-control numbering convention. I will not generate a compliant number until that is resolved.

steps.action: Collect governing evidence and determine whether a governed document-number convention applies.
steps.on_missing: Start the AI inquiry. Do not assume simplified numbering until the authority sweep is complete.

steps.action: Resolve numbering profile by precedence: law/regulation; contract/appointment; appointing-party/authority requirements; incorporated external/national standard; project information standard/EIR; BEP/CDE configuration; TIVERIT fallback.
Build a missing-field set from the selected profile and available project evidence.
Run the AI inquiry for unresolved fields, preferring BEP/project evidence and requesting focused user confirmation only where evidence is silent, ambiguous, or conflicting.

Classify the sheet/drawing semantic record: project phase, project stage, work condition, building/volume, zone/area, level/location, discipline, information form, content class, content subtype, sequence, status/suitability, revision, and title.
Echo normalized or user-confirmed project facts when interpretation was required and persist them for reuse across subsequent sheets.
Apply the selected profile to generate or validate the required document identity without changing the underlying semantic classification.
Run pre-registration validation against the selected authority/profile and CDE-required metadata.
If validation passes, permit technical registration in the CDE. Registration execution does not create or alter underlying approval/acceptance authority.
After formal registration or issue, route identity changes through governed document-control change/supersede procedure and preserve traceability.

failure_conditions: The AI invents a project code, client code, content range, or CDE field mapping instead of retrieving or asking for it.
The AI repeatedly asks for project-wide facts already established by the BEP or prior confirmed answers.
A user-provided project fact is falsely promoted to external-standard, client-enterprise, or contractual authority.
A TIVERIT fallback number is generated while a higher-precedence project convention is known or unresolved.
CDE platform configuration is treated as authority without a governing project basis.
Project stage is inferred from demolition/existing/proposed condition.
An enlarged floor plan is silently treated as a detail solely because a numbering range uses the same digit.
A document is first registered with an unresolved classification or number and expected to be casually renamed later.
A client/project profile is activated without curated governing evidence.
A public TIVERIT example exposes real project/client identifiers where neutral placeholders would preserve the rule.
